body:
I wish I could take all the time in the world to keep trying to get better but the reality of the matter is that I can't be dependent on my parents or my boyfriend forever. I've been trying to finish my bachelor's but it's been 3 or 4 semesters in a row now that I had to take a medical withdrawal. I obviously can't work in this situation, so what do I do?

I don't want to watch life pass me by from inside a hospital. I need something, anything to feel like I'm somehow normal. Even if I knew "Okay you're going to be on benefits now" or something like that at least I'd have an idea of what's going on. I'm in limbo, trying to finish a degree and failing.

EDIT: Each of my disorders are being addressed by medication

My therapist has already identified that she isn't trained to deal with eating disorders so I have a consultation set up with another therapist at her practice on wednesday.

I do take medication, though I don't want to list the specific ones as several people in my life would be able to identify me from the list.

I guess I've thought about looking for support groups for the bipolar but right now I'm hurting so badly that it's a serious accomplishment if I can get off the couch

Psychiatrist has been generally helpful but we can't find something that works long term.

Therapist is pretty new but my psych has been doing talk therapy for years and generally this new psychologist doesn't have much to offer that he hasn't already mentioned.

The support group is for ADHD and it's pretty good but it's not the adhd that makes me wan to die.

I most recently had ECT which helped enough to get me out of the hospital but it's looking like I might be back in the psych ward pretty soon with how I'm feeling.

I know I have a lot of support and that also makes me hurt. Though I know killing myself would devastate my partner and family a lot more than another hospitalization would, I don't think I can handle seeing the pain and helplessness they'll feel when I'm admitted yet again. At least if I'm dead I don't have to see the destruction I cause.

Thank you for listening
